why: A gym trainer on a retainer plus 35% of client session spend and 5% of referred members' fees, working 6 hours a day, 6 days a week, 49 weeks a year, is believable.
The routing split (47/37/16) and the fault pie (33/21/16/14/9/7) each sum to 100%, and 15,000 callers surveyed in a month is believable for a broadband provider.
A grocery wholesaler with $520 million sales, goods at 93% and operating costs at 9% losing 2% is consistent and believable for a thin-margin wholesaler.
Half-year spend of $30 to $95 per member at a tea subscription club is believable, and the question's fall/rise is a stated hypothetical.
Business-line revenues of EUR 44 to 238 million growing a few percent a year with margins of 3% to 12% are believable for a freight company.
Game prices of EUR 4 to 7, a few hundred bowlers per centre a week and EUR 10 of bar spend are believable, and a 35% bar margin against 15% for the sector is within a factor of a few.
Thermacor's heat pump share falling from about 14% to 11% of a $1.5 to $2.35 billion market, and about 19% of the boiler market, is believable.
Both pies sum to 100%, and 4,800 exit responses over four weeks is believable for a coastal-town aquarium.
180,000 new drivers with first-year profit of $0.50 to $20.50 on 90-day rental fees of $39 to $281 implies thin but believable car-sharing margins.
The group home counts add to the stated 31.5k (of about 40,000 homes), and GBP 9.75 million of repair cost over 85,000 jobs is believable for a housing association of that size.
